notes.title: Summer may have arrived outside… but deep in our dungeon? It’s cold. Very cold.
notes.content: [h2]What We’re Working On[/h2][p][/p][p]Summer may have arrived outside, flowers are blooming, birds are singing… but deep in our dungeon? It’s cold. Very cold. And not just because of the lack of sunlight.[/p][p]Lately, the halls have started to attract some particularly ravenous creatures. So while others are off enjoying picnics, we’re down here building traps and prepping fireballs.[/p][p][/p][h2]Monsters Incoming![/h2][p][/p][p]We’ve commissioned an external artist to bring new monsters to life. It’s not cheap - but let’s be honest, you can put a price on horror, and we just did.[/p][p]The results? Blood golems, zombies, strange abominations you’d never want to meet in a dark dungeon.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/d44c815f6a6baa12cc3c51ff3c0fe6fbf8415996.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]From Relics to Rubbish[/h2][p][/p][p]We’re working hard to get items into the game. Each one needs logic, visuals (icon + ground sprite), and a decent description. That´s lot of work.[/p][p]No cursed gear or mystery penalties here. We want players to feel curious, not paranoid. But in the future, we´d like to add some epic artifacts with unique powers and lore.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/1bb71d25e5167f3ff3da715e0e4e0f38c1ce52bf.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]The Music Saga[/h2][p][/p][p]We’re also hunting for a composer to create an original soundtrack. Turns out this is trickier than expected. Especially when one minute of custom music can cost up to $200. Since we estimate around 30 minutes of music, we’re currently figuring out what absolutely needs a theme and what can survive with slightly spooky silence.[/p][p][/p][h2]Mapping the World (Finally)[/h2][p][/p][p]Until now, we were mostly winging it. We’ve finally mapped out the full game world on paper - dungeons, key locations, and the main story arc.[/p][p][b]We’re not just building a floor-by-floor dungeon. We’re creating a small world you can freely explore, with choices in where to go and what to face.[/b][/p][p]Now we know where you’ll go, what horrors await, and most importantly where to drop the best cliffhangers. The chaos is finally getting a map.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/a967908ad05d8ff3c974841a58e8b9f13053ba26.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]That’s all for now![/h2][p][/p][p]Thanks for reading, thanks for your support, and thanks even more if you leave a comment or share the project with a fellow adventurer. It means the world to our small team![/p][p]What’s one monster that absolutely must be in any proper RPG? Drop your pick in the comments. Until next time, may your loot be shiny and your save files uncorrupted.[/p]

notes.title: Development update: Skills, demo and early access
notes.content:
[i]Hello adventurers… gather ‘round, we’ve got an update from the frontlines![/i]

[h1]What are we working on now?[/h1]

Development is forging ahead - and right now, we're tackling very critical elements. Hero Skills. Balancing the number, making them fun, and ensuring every skill feels meaningful? It's a boss fight of its own.

[i]Fun fact[/i]: Classic RPGs averaged 7–9 skills per hero – and we’re sticking to that spirit. Instead of diving into overly complex skill trees, we’ve chosen a more focused approach: classic levelable skills.

But don’t be fooled by the simplicity – we’re aiming for smarter design.
Take the warrior, for example: specializing early in axes might feel rewarding… until you stumble upon an epic sword. Oops. We’re working to minimize moments like that, without sacrificing depth or replayability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/fbc1fad7932871930e88c80eff518a0b7964dd36.jpg[/img]

Another key area we’re fine-tuning is combat complexity - things like stats, battle mechanics, and negative traits. Our goal is to hit a sweet spot: not overwhelming, but rich with proven RPG delights like [i]Burn, Bleed, Freeze, Stun,[/i] or [i]Poison[/i].

And yes - each class will feature [i]unique late-game specializations[/i] to unlock as you level up. We want your build choices to feel both personal and powerful. Unfortunately, most of these things are still on paper. Which brings us to the next point.

[h1]Demo delayed[/h1]

We’ve made the tough call to delay the demo to later this year. Right now, several critical elements just aren’t in place: music, events, and some key gameplay mechanics.

We’d rather show you something polished and exciting, than rush out a half-working version. We truly believe this is the right call – and we hope you’ll agree once you see what’s coming.

And good news: we’ve started working with a talented visual person who's helping us create [b]event graphic[/b]. These will breathe life into in-game events, offering both classic and unique choices inspired by old-school favorites like [i]Eye of the Beholder[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/c22ea423ced36b02ccb887d12e5c1967430677eb.jpg[/img]

Also with all the moving parts and the growing scope, the thought of doing an Early Access release has popped. Would that be something you’d be interested in?

As always – thanks for being part of this journey. Your support means the world.

notes.title: Legends never rest, and neither should you.
notes.content:
Let’s be honest - every good dungeon crawl starts the same way: with a locked door, zero context, and a party that looks like it was thrown together by a drunk wizard on a deadline. 

As we continue digging deeper into the cursed catacombs and haunted mines, it’s time to answer a question many of you have been asking: “[i]Who the heck am I bringing into this deathtrap with me?[/i]”

In the demo, you’ll be playing with a pre-built party to give you a taste of the game’s tone, mechanics and of course - [b]races[/b]. Today, we’re introducing two of them in detail.

[h2]HOREMOUNT – ROCK HARD, THINK SLOW[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/b7ec1046a6f23aaaf8082fe3db106a578100468b.jpg[/img]

If you ever wondered what it’s like to give a walking boulder a sword and a personal vendetta, meet the [b]Horemount[/b]. Towering stone warriors from the frostbitten northern mountains, these living slabs of granite have been forged by howling winds, freezing blizzards, and a complete lack of social skills.

They hit like falling anvils and shrug off damage like it’s an annoying breeze. Just don’t ask them to solve a riddle or use a magic scroll - they’ll either stare blankly or eat it.

Let’s be honest: you guessed this guy’s gonna be your [b]Warrior[/b]. Big health pool, big hammer, small attention span. But hey, somebody has to stand in front of the traps and take the arrow to the stone.

[h2]RAVEN – MUTANT LIZARD THING WITH ISSUES[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45212250/40681e77fa9a08672fec7e434b6dd9ad435d3809.jpg[/img]

Say hello to the [b]Raven[/b]. This race of lizard mutants hails from a land so toxic, even the mushrooms wear gas masks. Every Raven is a grab bag of strange mutations - some grow extra eyes, others spit acid, and some... spontaneously combust. We’re still figuring that one out.

The cool part? No two Ravens are ever exactly the same. Each playthrough, your Raven might have different resistances, senses, or weird biological “features”.

[h2]What about normal people?[/h2]

We hear some of you saying: “Alright, that’s cool and all, but what if I [i]don’t[/i] want to play as a rock brute or a rogue cockroach?”

Don’t worry - we haven’t forgotten the good old classic fantasy races. In the full game, you can absolutely expect to see the likes of the [b]Human [/b](the jack-of-all-trades, master of none, hero of many), the [b]Dwarf[/b] and yes - something [b]Elf-adjacent[/b].

So tell us – what is your favourite race you usually play or you wish to see?

Until next time: watch your step and remember - if the chest has teeth, maybe don’t open it.
